subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
By the county each hospital sits in, as CMS records it.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did - the Medical Center have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: About 6.0 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Highland Hills Medical Center have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: About 4.7 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians trained at - the Medical Center in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Delta Health System's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From 2 of the 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024; the others had no full year on file.

questions.q: What percent of - the Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 30 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 33 percent.

questions.q: What percent of - the Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 14 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 0 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Delta Health System's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Delta Health System's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.why: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2024, what percent of Highland Hills Medical Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Delta Health System run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in Mississippi. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: How many of Delta Health System's hospitals are outside a metropolitan area?
questions.why: They are - the Medical Center and Northwest Missississippi Regional Medical Center.

questions.q: How many beds do Delta Health System's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From 2 of the 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024; the others had no full year on file.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Delta Health System's hospitals report in a year, added together?
questions.why: About 8 a day. From 2 of the 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024; the others had no full year on file.
